source_text: Ὁ δὲ ἡγεμὼν λέγει τῷ μάρτυρι· Εἰπέ μοι, ἄνθρωπε, πόθεν εἶ, ἢ ποίου γένους τυγχάνεις, ἢ τί τὸ ὄνομά σου; Κόνων εἶπεν· Πόλεως μέν εἰμι ἐγὼ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, συγγένεια δέ μοί ἐστιν πρὸς Χριστόν, ὃν ἐκ προγόνων λατρεύω, ὃν ἔγνωκα ἐπὶ πάντων θεῶν.
thought_title: Conon names his home and kinship to Christ
orientation: The governor now questions Conon directly about where he is from, his family, and his name.
pass_a_gloss: And the governor says to the martyr: Tell me, man, from where are you, or of what family do you happen to be, or what is your name? Conon said: I am of a city, Nazareth of Galilee, and there is kinship to me toward Christ, whom from ancestors I worship, whom I have known above all gods.

choices.why: keeps literal preposition and noun rather than smoothing to relative
keeps source order and force of ancestral worship stated in brief

pass_b_english: The governor says to the martyr, "Tell me, man, where are you from, what family do you belong to, and what is your name?" Conon said, "I am from the city of Nazareth in Galilee, and my kinship is toward Christ, whom I worship from my ancestors and whom I have known as above all gods."
